name: io.watchfor/watchfor
title: WatchFor
description: Uptime & infrastructure monitoring: monitors, incidents, status pages, live diagnostics.

tools.name: get_summary
tools.description: Snapshot of the organization right now: monitors by effective status (up / down / degraded / paused / unknown, active count, health score), hosts running the agent (online / stale / offline / never), the combined fleet health, open incidents by severity, incidents started in the last 24 h, open maintenance windows, attention items (monitors with no notification route) and certificate and domain expiry across every SSL and RDAP monitor (counts plus the ten soonest). One call covers the whole organization, however many monitors it has.

tools.name: get_incident_stats
tools.description: Aggregate incident statistics over a period: totals by severity, MTTR (mean time to resolve), MTBF, the five most unstable monitors, and counts[] per hour (24h) or per day (UTC, oldest first). Each bucket has a display label (bucket, like "Nov 13", no year) and bucket_start (ISO 8601, the sortable value).

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Org report for a period, always compared with the previous equal-length period: uptime, incidents, MTTR/MTBF, downtime, response-time trend, per-monitor rows (worst first), type-aware sections (SSL/domain expiry, Core Web Vitals, heartbeat check-ins, DNS blocklists, MCP tool drift, hosts running the agent) and plain-language insights. The same engine behind the dashboard Reports page and scheduled report emails. Uptime and incidents cover any period; check success and response times only the plan's chart history (meta.history says when a period was cut).

from.description: Custom period start, ISO 8601 (advanced-reports plans only; max 92 days)

monitor_ids.description: Scope to these monitor IDs (advanced plans; union with tags)

tags.description: Scope to monitors carrying any of these tags (advanced plans)

sections.description: Only these type-aware sections (advanced plans; omitted = all)

incident_status.description: Count only incidents in any of these lifecycle states toward the incident numbers (counts, MTTR/MTTA, per-monitor incidents); uptime and downtime always count every critical incident. Omitted = all (advanced plans)

tools.name: get_report_schedules
tools.description: The organization's two scheduled report-email cadences (weekly + monthly): enabled state, recipients (max 5) and any recipients who unsubscribed themselves.

tools.name: set_report_schedule
tools.description: Enables or disables the weekly or monthly report email and/or replaces its recipient list (up to 5 addresses). Enabling needs at least one recipient; clearing the recipients disables the cadence; adding the first recipient to an empty, disabled cadence enables it automatically.

enabled.description: Turn the cadence on or off

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Current subscription plan with limits (-1 = unlimited, 0 = feature off) and live usage counts. usage.monitors_by_type matches limits.max_monitors_by_type (browser = page speed / Core Web Vitals, playwright = scripted browser checks; usage.browser_checks is the playwright count). Feature limits the monitor config is checked against: allow_ssl_grade (SSL trackTlsGrade), max_playwright_timeout_seconds, max_playwright_locations, playwright_test_runs_per_hour, max_integrity_pages_per_monitor, max_integrity_browser_monitors, allow_integrity_script_content.

tools.name: list_monitors
tools.description: Lists monitors, cursor-paginated, as slim items: id, name, type, target, status, tags (config and the full detail are in the single-monitor read). Filters: type, status, tag, and q (a substring of name or target).

q.description: Case-insensitive substring search over name and target

type.description: Monitor type, e.g. http, dns, ssl, playwright (browser checks), browser (Core Web Vitals)

status.description: Effective status: down = confirmed critical incident open; degraded = a failing check or alert rule not yet confirmed, or an open warning incident

tools.name: get_monitor
tools.description: One monitor by id: config, available_metrics (the alert metrics valid for its type), last_check and `latest`: what the latest check found, in the terms of its type (certificate days left, domain status, blocklist listings, SPF/DMARC/DKIM, Core Web Vitals, failing test step, NTP offset, UDP/game packet loss and jitter, MCP tool count…; kind = the monitor type).

tools.name: get_monitor_types
tools.description: Discovery catalog of all 31 monitor types: target format, default alert rules, per-type alert metrics (exact `metric` strings, operators, value types) and config fields: the values monitors and alert rules are validated against. `type` returns just that type (much smaller). Type `playwright` = browser checks (scripted Playwright journeys); type `browser` = Core Web Vitals (Lighthouse audit of one page).

type.description: Only this monitor type, e.g. http or ssl; omitted = the whole catalog

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.description: Creates a monitor (write scope). `type` is a type from the monitor-type catalog, and `target` and `config` follow that type's target format and config fields: config is validated against the type (wrong values are rejected with the field path; keys the type does not use are dropped). `locations` are probe location ids. Interval is in seconds and is validated against the plan's per-type minimum. Name is at most 50 characters; up to 10 tags. is_paused: true creates it paused; scheduling_strategy is roundrobin (default), random or parallel. Targets in private, loopback or link-local address space are rejected. clone_from_monitor_id (cloneFromMonitorId also works) copies the source's alert rules and config, and any omitted field takes the source's value; the clone is validated like a new monitor, so a copied setting a create would refuse (an sftp source without username) is a 400 naming it, and that value then goes in config. Credentials (config fields marked secret: mailbox/SMTP/FTP passwords, SSH keys) are write-only: stored encrypted and returned as "[redacted]". Mail types: imap, pop3, smtp (optional login on 587/465), email_roundtrip (interval ≥ 300 s).

type.description: Monitor type from the monitor-type catalog: playwright = browser check (Playwright script), browser = Core Web Vitals (Lighthouse)

target.description: What to check, in the type's target format; required for every type but heartbeat, whose ping URL the server assigns (ping_url in the result). smtp: hostname only, port in config.port

interval.description: Check interval in seconds. Omitted: the dashboard's default for the type — 60 s (page integrity 900, email round trip 600), raised to the plan's minimum for the type; a heartbeat has none — it follows config.periodSeconds / cronExpression

locations.description: Probe location ids. At least one is required, except for heartbeat monitors, which take none.

config.description: Type-specific settings: the config fields of the type

clone_from_monitor_id.description: Clone this monitor (same type): its alert rules, config and — when omitted here — target, interval, locations, tags are copied

is_paused.description: true = create it paused (no checks until it is resumed); default false

scheduling_strategy.description: How the locations take turns: roundrobin (default, one location per check in turn), random, or parallel (every location on every check — plan-gated)

tools.name: update_monitor
tools.description: Updates a monitor (write scope); only the fields sent change. config is merged into the stored config: an omitted key is kept, a key set to null is removed, any other value replaces it (arrays and nested objects whole); the result is validated against the monitor type. description: null clears it. confirmationThreshold / durationWindow / notificationGroupIds in config apply to every alert rule of the monitor (null resets each rule to its own default; notificationGroupIds: [] = nobody is notified; an id that is not one of the organization's contact groups is refused by name). Setting a value that drives an alert preset (body match, expectedValues, …) creates or switches on its rule; removing it switches the rule off. HTTP body match: config.keywordValue (+ keywordMode contains|not_contains, keywordPatternType text|wildcard|regex, keywordCaseInsensitive) is compiled into the regexp the check evaluates, like the dashboard card; failIfBodyNotMatchesRegexp / failIfBodyMatchesRegexp are the raw form, and both with different meanings is a 400. Expiry reminders: config.expiryReminderDays, e.g. [14, 3] (whole days 1–365, up to 5; http, api, mcp, ssl and rdap) re-notifies an open, unacknowledged certificate/domain expiry incident once when that many days are left. Write-only credentials (password, smtpPassword, receivePassword, privateKey, HTTP/API/MCP authPassword, bearerToken and credential request-header values) and requestBody read back as "[redacted]": an omitted secret or an echoed "[redacted]" keeps the stored value, the mask is never stored as a new value, and a header mask with nothing stored is a 400. {{NAME}} in an auth field, header value or body reads an organization variable or secret (Settings → Variables) instead of a literal secret. Changing the server, port, TLS mode or login a password is used with (for HTTP/API/MCP the URL host, port or scheme, or the basic-auth username), or setting verifyTls to false, requires the credential again in the same call, else 400 "Re-enter the …". The result carries check_queued: true when the change (target, port, credentials, TLS, request…) dispatched one immediate check, not counted against Run now.

target.description: What to check, in the type's target format

description.description: Free-text note, up to 500 characters; null clears it

interval.description: Check interval in seconds, at least the plan's minimum

locations.description: Probe location ids: at least one, except on a heartbeat, which has none (omitted or [])

config.description: Config keys to change, merged into the stored config

tools.name: set_monitor_paused
tools.description: Pauses or resumes a monitor (write scope). Idempotent. Resuming starts one immediate check (check_queued: true): at most one per monitor per 10 minutes and 20 per organization a minute, a budget separate from on-demand checks; otherwise next_check_at says by when the first scheduled check runs.

tools.name: delete_monitor
tools.description: Deletes a monitor permanently (write scope), together with its scheduled checks, alert rules and open incidents. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: run_check_now
tools.description: Dispatches one immediate on-demand check for a monitor (write scope, plan-limited per hour). Its result appears in the monitor's check results within about a minute.

tools.name: reset_monitor_history
tools.description: Irreversible (write scope): deletes a monitor's entire recorded history: every check and latency record, every incident with its timeline, delivery history, internal notes, post-mortems and auto-published status-page incidents, plus the alerting engine's failure counters. The monitor itself is kept with its configuration, alert rules, tags and locations and keeps checking; uptime starts over from the reset (the dashboard shows 'since reset'). Cannot be undone. Returns the counts of what was deleted.

tools.name: get_integrity_baseline
tools.description: Page integrity monitors only: the accepted baseline each watched page is compared against: per page whether it has one, when it was captured and how (auto = first check, manual = accepted in the dashboard, api = accepted over the API or MCP, timer = auto-accepted after the monitor's autoAcceptAfterHours), plus trusted_origins, the text-change threshold and fresh_accept (the latest fresh accept: pending, accepted, expired or failed). 404 for other monitor types.

tools.name: accept_integrity_baseline
tools.description: Page integrity monitors only (write scope): accepts what the newest check saw as the new baseline, for all watched pages or only `pages`, so an intended change (a deploy, a new vendor script) stops alerting. Everything that check saw becomes the normal state, including security findings (new script sources, changed code, new form targets). When nothing else differs, the open integrity incidents resolve at once (incidents_resolved); otherwise a check starts right away (check_requested) and they close on it. fresh: true checks the pages first and accepts that check (waits up to ~85 s; status pending = still running, the accept then finishes on its own and the baseline's fresh_accept reports how it ended). Pages a check could not fetch come back in `skipped`.

pages.description: Watched page URLs to accept; omitted = all

fresh.description: true = the pages are checked first and that check is accepted (for a change deployed moments ago)

tools.name: set_expected_change_window
tools.description: Release marker for an MCP monitor (write scope, owner/admin): from now and for the next `window_minutes` (1–60, default 15), tool-inventory drift on that monitor doesn't open an incident; the change is recorded in the drift timeline as "Expected — release marker". Only its Tool Inventory Changed rule is covered, so downtime still alerts, and drift after the window ends alerts as usual. Each call records a new marker; 12 per hour per monitor. Returns starts_at, ends_at and the rules covered.

tools.name: test_playwright_script
tools.description: Browser checks: runs a Playwright Test script once in a sandboxed browser without saving it (write scope; counts against the plan's test runs per hour). The script is a normal `@playwright/test` file: `import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'`, `test.step(...)` for readable steps, `process.env.TARGET_URL` for the site and `process.env.NAME` for organization variables and secrets. It runs with those secrets in its environment and can reach any public host. A script error returns 400 naming the line. Waits up to ~60 s and returns the run (status passed/flaky/failed/timed_out/script_error/infra_error, failed step with its error and code frame, console errors, failed requests, Web Vitals) plus missing_variables: the process.env names the organization hasn't set, which are unset when the script runs. A run still going after that returns its test_run_id instead.

location_id.description: A probe location id with browser support; omitted = the nearest

tools.name: get_playwright_run
tools.description: Browser checks: one run in detail: monitor_id + run_id for a scheduled or Run-now run of a browser-check monitor, or test_run_id for a one-off test run. Returns steps (status, duration, error message + code frame), the failure, console and page errors, failed and blocked requests, Web Vitals per page, runtime versions, presigned screenshot URLs (15 min) and the trace-viewer link.

run_id.description: A scheduled or Run-now run of that monitor

test_run_id.description: A one-off test run, in place of monitor_id + run_id

tools.name: list_playwright_runs
tools.description: Browser checks: a check's runs, newest first: status (passed / flaky / failed / timed_out / script_error / infra_error = could not run on our side, never an incident), duration, failed step, console-error and failed-request counts. status=failed or status=flaky narrows the list. 404 for monitors that are not browser checks.

status.description: Only failed or flaky runs; default all

tools.name: get_monitor_uptime
tools.description: Uptime for a monitor over a period — confirmed critical incidents only (the same formula as the dashboard; failed checks that never became an incident do not count), plus check success ratio, check totals and response-time stats; scheduled maintenance excluded. Uptime is null when nothing was observed (no check since the monitor was created or reset, or paused for the whole period) — no data, not 100. Response-time fields cover successful checks only and are null when none succeeded. Heartbeat monitors: /start pings are events, not checks — left out of the check totals and the success ratio.

tools.name: get_suggested_thresholds
tools.description: Alert thresholds for a network-distance metric (one marked region_scoped: true in the monitor-type catalog: latency, packet loss, jitter) suggested from the monitor's own checks: per region it is checked from, the p95 over its history up to 7 days (`window`), the suggested warning and critical, which region the all-regions values come from (most locations) and which regions need a rule of their own. `method` spells out the metric's formula (slow operations: max(p95 × 1.5, p95 + 30 ms, p99 × 1.2) / max(p95 × 2.5, p95 + 80 ms, p99 × 2); packet loss moves in whole packet steps, see packets_per_check). Read-only: no rule is created or changed. ready=false until a region has enough checks; 400 for a metric that isn't region-scoped or isn't measured.

metric.description: A region-scoped metric of the monitor's type (e.g. response_time, game.query_rtt_ms) or a family: latency, packet_loss, jitter. Omitted = the type's first (game: latency).

tools.name: get_monitor_checks
tools.description: Recent check results for a monitor (status, latency, per-location performance), newest first, each with its run_id. Each row names where it ran as location_id / location_name (location is the prober's internal name, deprecated). success=false returns only failed checks, success=true only passing ones. hours widens the window (up to 720, and never past the plan's check history: a longer window is cut and the result carries history_notice). When there is more than one page, has_more is true and next_cursor, sent back as cursor with the same filters, returns the next one. Heartbeat rows carry event: start (a /start ping: a run began, not a check-in; not counted in the per-location figures), finish, fail or missed.

success.description: false = only failed checks, true = only passing

tools.name: get_check_details
tools.description: Everything the probe saw on one check run: the full recorded result (HTTP headers and timings, TLS chain and grade, DNS answers, assertion outcomes, the error) with sensitive values redacted server-side. run_id is the run_id of a row in the monitor's check results. The same detail the dashboard's probe-result view shows. A check older than the plan's check history is not found.

run_id.description: The run_id of a row in the monitor's check results

tools.name: list_locations
tools.description: Probe locations available to the organization, with the ids that monitor locations and location_id arguments take.

tools.name: list_alert_rules
tools.description: A monitor's alert rules (system defaults + custom), each with its id. Rules define when incidents fire.

tools.name: create_alert_rule
tools.description: Creates an alert rule on a monitor (write scope). `metric` is one of the monitor type's alert metrics (the catalog's exact strings, also listed in the monitor's available_metrics); value is always a string. At most one rule per metric per severity per region scope: a duplicate is refused (409) and the existing rule stays as it is. Network-distance rules (metrics marked region_scoped: true in the catalog: latency, packet loss, jitter): `regions` limits the rule to checks from those regions (e.g. a latency threshold for Europe only); Offline and every other rule are judged from every region and refuse regions; a region-scoped rule takes precedence over an all-regions one of the same metric and severity. failure_threshold omitted: the monitor's confirmationThreshold when it has one, else the count the dashboard's Alerting tab gives the rule: 3 on a region-scoped metric, a card's own count where it has one (Domain Expiry, certificate expiry, RBL listing: 1), else the type's default (3 on most types) (durationWindow likewise follows the monitor's). The response's `warnings` (empty when fine) says when the saved rule can never fire as the monitor is set up: a region it isn't checked from, or a metric only measured with a setting that is off (e.g. packet loss with packetLoss off).

metric.description: Exact metric string from the catalog

operator.description: Comparison operator: > < >= <= == != for numbers, in_groups/not_in_groups for status codes

value.description: Threshold as a string, e.g. "2000", "14", or '["2xx","3xx"]' for status groups

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failing checks before an incident opens

min_failed_probes.description: Locations that must report the failure in the same evaluation (default 1)

duration_window.description: Seconds the condition must hold before the rule fires (0 = fire on the confirmed failure; omitted: the monitor's own setting on create, unchanged on update)

contact_group_id.description: Contact group id this rule notifies, in addition to the monitor's own groups (null removes it on update)

regions.description: Network-distance rules only (region_scoped: true): region slugs the rule is judged from (europe, north-america, south-america, asia, middle-east, africa, oceania). Omitted = all regions. Refused on Offline and every other rule.

tools.name: update_alert_rule
tools.description: Updates an alert rule (write scope): a threshold, the severity, enabled, or any other field sent; the rest stay. metric/operator/value are validated against the monitor type's catalog. A system rule (is_system) keeps what it watches: the Up/Down rule's condition and a type default's metric can't change (400). The response's `warnings` (empty when fine) says when the rule can never fire as the monitor is set up.

metric.description: Exact metric string from the catalog

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failing checks before an incident opens

min_failed_probes.description: Locations that must report the failure in the same evaluation (default 1)

duration_window.description: Seconds the condition must hold before the rule fires (0 = fire on the confirmed failure; omitted: the monitor's own setting on create, unchanged on update)

contact_group_id.description: Contact group id this rule notifies, in addition to the monitor's own groups (null removes it on update)

regions.description: Network-distance rules only (region_scoped: true): region slugs the rule is judged from. Omitted = unchanged; null or [] = all regions. Refused on Offline and every other rule.

enabled.description: false switches the rule off, true back on

tools.name: delete_alert_rule
tools.description: Deletes a custom alert rule permanently (write scope). System default rules cannot be deleted (403); they can be switched off with enabled: false.

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: Alert recipients (people) with their group memberships: who gets notified. Cursor-paginated.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: One contact by id: name, email address, phone number and the contact groups they are a member of.

tools.name: create_contact
tools.description: Creates an alert recipient (write scope), optionally placed straight into contact groups (group_ids). A duplicate email (case-insensitive) is refused as a conflict with the existing contact.

group_ids.description: Contact groups to add the contact to

tools.name: update_contact
tools.description: Updates a contact (write scope); only the fields sent change. group_ids replaces all memberships ([] removes them from every group, omitted keeps them).

group_ids.description: Every contact group the contact is in (replaces them)

tools.name: delete_contact
tools.description: Deletes a contact permanently (write scope) and removes them from every contact group. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_contact_groups
tools.description: Contact groups (notification groups): where alerts are delivered, with the ids a monitor's config.notificationGroupIds and an alert rule's contact group refer to. Cursor-paginated.

tools.name: get_contact_group
tools.description: One contact group in detail, including its member list (who exactly gets paged).

tools.name: create_contact_group
tools.description: Creates a contact group (write scope), optionally with initial members (contact ids).

tools.name: update_contact_group
tools.description: Updates a contact group (write scope). contact_ids replaces the full member list ([] empties the group, omitted keeps it).

tools.name: delete_contact_group
tools.description: Deletes a contact group permanently (write scope). The organization's default group, and a group still used by monitors, alert rules or notification channels, are refused with 409 (with the counts) and nothing is deleted.

tools.name: list_status_pages
tools.description: The organization's public status pages, all of them in one list: id, slug, public URL, visibility and what each currently says (overall_status). Components and their status are in each page's detail.

tools.name: get_status_page
tools.description: One status page with what visitors see right now: overall_status, every component with its status and the monitors and hosts behind it (tag rules resolved), its public_cause (how much auto-published notices explain: hidden / cause / full), third-party mirrors, and the incident count.

tools.name: list_announcements
tools.description: Announcements published on a status page — incidents and scheduled maintenance as customers saw them, with their update timeline (investigating → identified → monitoring → resolved), scheduled start/end and the internal incident they came from.

tools.name: get_on_call
tools.description: Who is on call right now and until when, who is next (upcoming shifts), the schedule's layers and participants, active overrides, and whether the current person can actually be paged (reachable).

tools.name: list_notification_channels
tools.description: Where alerts are delivered: every notification channel (Slack, Discord, Telegram, PagerDuty, email, webhook, …) with its type, enabled flag, severity filter, the contact groups routed to it, and a redacted config — tokens and webhook secrets never appear.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: Incidents, newest first (cursor-paginated). Filters: status (firing/acknowledged/resolved), severity, a single monitor (monitor_id) and a started_at time range (since/until). Each incident carries the rule that fired (name/metric/operator/value) and duration_seconds.

since.description: ISO 8601 — incidents started at/after this time

until.description: ISO 8601 — incidents started before this time

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Full detail of one incident: the humanised message, the fire-time rule, root_cause (expected vs detected — e.g. 'HTTP Status Code = 404'), also_failing (the monitor's other rules the same failed checks tripped, held into this one incident), the trigger snapshot (metrics the probe reported, which locations confirmed — location_id / location_name; the prober fields are deprecated), fire_count and the event timeline. fire_count is 1 when the incident opens and grows by one with each keep-alive refresh from the alerting engine (about hourly) while it stays open — not separate firings, incidents or notifications.

tools.name: acknowledge_incident
tools.description: Acknowledges a firing incident (write scope): repeat notifications pause while someone investigates.

tools.name: resolve_incident
tools.description: Manually resolves an incident (write scope). Accepted asynchronously: the alerting engine's failure state is reset, and if the underlying problem persists the incident re-fires.

tools.name: accept_expected_change
tools.description: Drift incidents only, an MCP monitor's Tool Inventory Changed (write scope, owner/admin): marks the tool change as intended, e.g. a release that added or reworded tools. An open incident is resolved (asynchronously; the channels get "resolved — accepted as an expected change"); either way the accept is recorded on the incident timeline, on the monitor's drift timeline ("Accepted as expected by …") and in the Activity log. `note` (up to 500 characters) says why. Any other incident → 400. An unexplained tool description change can also be an MCP rug-pull.

tools.name: set_incident_uptime_exclusion
tools.description: Marks a resolved incident as a false positive (excluded: true, write scope) or removes that mark (excluded: false). An excluded incident stays on record with its timeline, notes and post-mortem, but is left out of uptime, SLA, reports and the public status page; `reason` (up to 500 characters) records why it was not real downtime. Excluding an incident that is still firing or acknowledged fails with HTTP 409. Returns the updated incident with excluded_from_uptime, exclusion_reason, excluded_by and excluded_at.

excluded.description: true = exclude from uptime (false positive), false = include again

reason.description: Why it was not real downtime, up to 500 characters

tools.name: get_postmortem
tools.description: The incident's post-mortem (plan feature): title, status (draft/completed), is_public, severity (minor/major/critical), root_cause_category, `sections` (summary, impact, root_cause, detection, resolution, what_went_well, what_could_have_gone_better: text under each heading, "" when empty), the full markdown-lite `body`, author-added `timeline` entries and `action_items`. Returns { postmortem: null } when the incident has none yet. The incident's own events and root cause belong to the incident, not to the post-mortem.

tools.name: update_postmortem
tools.description: Creates or fills the incident's post-mortem draft (write scope; any member may, as in the dashboard). Creates it with the dashboard template on first use, then applies only the fields sent: `sections` replaces just the sections named (markdown-lite: **bold**, `code`, "- " lists, ### sub-headings; "" empties one; other sections and custom headings stay untouched); title, severity (minor/major/critical: the impact), root_cause_category, status (draft/completed); `add_timeline` [{at ISO 8601, text}] and `add_action_items` [{title, due_date?}] append, skipping exact repeats. The incident's automatic events (started/acknowledged/resolved) already show in the post-mortem without timeline entries. Publishing to the status page and deleting are not available here (owner/admin, dashboard). Returns the post-mortem.

severity.description: Impact: minor, major or critical; null clears it

root_cause_category.description: Root cause category; null clears it

sections.description: Text per section: summary, impact, root_cause, detection, resolution, what_went_well, what_could_have_gone_better

what_went_well.description: The what went well section text

what_could_have_gone_better.description: The what could have gone better section text

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: Alerting delivery history: every notification attempt with channel, delivery status (sent/failed/silenced), severity, incident and monitor, so whether an alert went out and which deliveries fail. Filters: status, channel_type, monitor_id, incident_id and a time range.

channel_type.description: e.g. telegram, slack, email, webhook, pagerduty

tools.name: list_activity
tools.description: The organization's audit trail: who changed what and when (monitors, alert rules, contacts, maintenance, channels; dashboard and API actions), for lining incidents up with recent config changes. Filters: entity_type / entity_id, a time range and q.

q.description: Free-text search — reaches action, actor name/email and the JSON change details (same as the dashboard search)

entity_type.description: e.g. monitor, alert_rule, contact, contact_group, maintenance_window, notification_channel, api_key

tools.name: list_hosts
tools.description: Servers running watchfor-agent, with liveness (online / stale = no batch for three push intervals, never sooner than 90 s / offline = none for 10 min / never = not reported yet) and the latest CPU, memory and disk gauges. status filters by liveness. A host's monitor_id is the id status-page components, maintenance windows and incident filters expect, and the id its uptime and alert rules are read and changed by; every other monitor read or change answers not found for it.

tools.name: get_host
tools.description: One host: OS, kernel, agent version, hardware, addresses (private, public, and the one it reports from), current CPU / memory / disk gauges and its monitor_id.

tools.name: get_host_metrics
tools.description: Metric time series for a host over 1h–30d, bucketed like the host page's charts. Metric names are the agent's catalogue: cpu.usage_pct, cpu.iowait_pct, cpu.steal_pct, load.1, mem.used_pct, swap.used_bytes, disk.used_pct (per mount), disk.inodes_used_pct, diskio.read_bytes_per_s, net.rx_bytes_per_s, net.tx_bytes_per_s (per interface), proc.total, sys.uptime_s.

tools.name: list_maintenance_windows
tools.description: Scheduled maintenance windows, most recent first, each with its state (active / upcoming / ended / disabled) and next_run_at. state=active returns the windows running now, state=upcoming the future ones; ended and disabled windows are in the unfiltered list.

state.description: Only windows running now, or only future ones

tools.name: create_maintenance_window
tools.description: Schedules a maintenance window (write scope): by default alerts are suppressed, the covered monitors show as under maintenance and the window's downtime is excluded from uptime; each can be switched off. One-time unless recurrence is set. Times are ISO 8601; duration in minutes.

monitor_tags.description: Tag-based targeting — auto-includes future matching monitors

recurrence.description: Repeat the window (default once); daily/weekly/monthly repeat at the start's local time in timezone

recurrence_until.description: ISO 8601 — no occurrence starts after this time

suppress_alerts.description: Hold notifications during the window (default true)

mark_maintenance.description: Show the covered monitors as under maintenance (default true)

exclude_from_sla.description: Leave the window's downtime out of uptime and SLA figures (default true)

tools.name: delete_maintenance_window
tools.description: Cancels a maintenance window permanently (write scope): it is removed with its future occurrences, and any active silences are lifted. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_diagnostics
tools.description: Catalog of the live checks WatchFor can run from its probe fleet, with the question each answers, its exact option names, and this organization's remaining allowance for each.

tools.name: diagnose_target
tools.description: Investigates a host or URL in one call: DNS, DNS propagation across every location, TLS grade, HTTP headers, and ping from up to 3 different regions, run in parallel and returned as one verdict (a status per check plus a machine-readable list of what looks wrong), with the TLS and security headers grades in `grades`. Each underlying check spends its own allowance, and a check the plan blocks comes back as skipped rather than failing the call. Needs a plan with location selection. Write scope.

target.description: Hostname or URL, e.g. example.com or https://example.com

max_locations.description: How many regions to ping from (default 3)

location_ids.description: Ping location ids, in place of one location per region
